title: Ivo and the Wolf
premise: Ines Winterbourne, exiled for a storm she swears she never called, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things — bottled grief, borrowed years, doors to nowhere. When prayers start being answered by old gods everyone believed dead, Ines discovers her own name in an ancient ledger of debts owed to them, and meets Ivo, a wolf-shaped god who remembers her from before her exile. Together they must find the door out of a country that was erased from maps and memory alike, pursued by the guild's collectors and a rival god who wants the door sealed forever. In the end, Ines chooses not to escape but to pay her debt by unmaking her exile's lie, restoring the country's name at the cost of her storm-calling — and Ivo, freed from godhood, walks out beside her as simply a wolf.
about_author: Zephyrine Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete maps and now writes fantasies about places that refuse to stay forgotten. They live near a cold coastline and insist the weather there is personal.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She catalogs a shipment of bottled grief for the Vellum Guild, revealing her meticulous nature and her exile's quiet shame. A collector brings in a strange item: a prayer scroll that answered itself. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: What the Gods Owe
chapters.summary: Ines finds her own name in a pre-exile ledger, listed as debtor to gods thought extinct. Her mentor Halvard warns her to burn the page; she copies it instead. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: dread mixed with a hunger for the truth of her past.

chapters.title: A Wolf at the Counting House
chapters.summary: A wolf appears in the guild's vaults, speaking with the voice of something old. He calls himself Ivo and claims he knew Ines before her exile. POV: Ines, with a brief Ivo interlude. Emotional beat: wary fascination, first spark of belonging.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered in Ashvale
chapters.summary: News spreads: across the city of Ashvale, small miracles are occurring — wells refilling, dead orchards blooming. The guild smells profit; Ines smells catastrophe. POV: alternating street-level vignettes and Ines. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Collector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane orders Ines to broker a contract with the returning gods, selling miracles on commission. She refuses; he threatens to expose the true record of her exile. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: cornered defiance.

chapters.title: Ivo's Memory of Rain
chapters.summary: Ivo tells Ines what really happened the night of her banishment: the storm was called to hide a god-murder, and she was made scapegoat. POV: Ivo, framed as told memory. Emotional beat: grief, and the first taste of justice outside any law.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Ivo reveals the erased nation of Vel Sarenne — struck from maps, its people scattered, its gods bound. The door out of it lies in Ines's ledger-debt. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity; her exile suddenly has geography.

chapters.title: Debts and Denials
chapters.summary: Corvane dispatches collectors to seize Ivo as guild property. Ines falsifies the ledgers to hide him, committing her first true crime against the guild. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: The Rival God
chapters.summary: Introduce Mavros, the god who survived Vel Sarenne's fall by betraying it, now feeding on the new answered prayers. He offers Ines freedom if she helps seal the door forever. POV: Mavros, then Ines. Emotional beat: seductive corruption.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Salt Marshes
chapters.summary: Ines and Ivo flee Ashvale ahead of the collectors, crossing haunted marshlands where the erased country bleeds through. POV: dual. Emotional bond deepens; Ivo weakens away from his old ground. Emotional beat: tenderness under pursuit.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: They reach a settlement of Vel Sarenne exiles who keep forbidden rites. An elder recognizes Ines's family name and gives her her mother's storm-token. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: belonging offered, and feared.

chapters.title: Halvard's Confession
chapters.summary: Halvard catches up, confessing he helped forge the exile record to protect Ines from Mavros's hunters — and that her mother died sealing the original door. POV: Halvard. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with love.

chapters.title: What Storms Are For
chapters.summary: Ines attempts to call a storm for the first time since exile and fails catastrophically, nearly killing Ivo. She realizes her power was never hers alone — it was lent by Vel Sarenne's sky. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: humbling, identity shaken to roots.

chapters.title: The Collectors Close
chapters.summary: Corvane's collectors raid the village, taking hostages including the elder. Ines can buy their lives only by surrendering the ledger-page bearing her debt. POV: Ivo watching Ines choose. Emotional beat: sacrifice without guarantee.

chapters.title: Mavros's Cathedral of Answers
chapters.summary: Mavros has built a cathedral where every prayer is answered — at the price of the asker's memories of home. Ines sees what 'belonging' bought cheaply becomes. POV: Ines inside the cathedral. Emotional beat: horror of easy grace.

chapters.title: The Terms of the Door
chapters.summary: Reading the debt-clause fully, Ines learns the door opens only for one who pays in full: a name restored, a lie unmade, a power relinquished. Ivo begs her to let him pay instead. POV: dual. Emotional beat: love arguing with duty.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Threshold
chapters.summary: They reach the door site; Mavros springs his trap, revealing Corvane has been his vessel all along. Halvard dies holding the collectors off. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: rage and loss fusing into resolve.

chapters.title: Ivo Unbound
chapters.summary: Ivo burns most of his divinity to shatter Mavros's hold on the door, collapsing into ordinary wolf-shape. Mavros, wounded, tries to seal the door from within. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: godhood traded for devotion.

chapters.title: The Payment
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Ines speaks her true name into the ledger, renounces her storm-calling, and declares the exile a lie before witnesses living and dead. The door opens; the erased country's name returns to the world. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: climax — justice rendered outside any court.

chapters.title: Mavros's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Inside the restored borders, the old gods' debts come due; Mavros is claimed by the land he betrayed, unmade into rain over Vel Sarenne. Corvane, mortal again, flees. POV: shifting chorus. Emotional beat: awe and terrible fairness.

chapters.title: Ledgers Closed
chapters.summary: Ines, powerless but named, rebuilds the village's records and is asked to stay as keeper of Vel Sarenne's recovered archive. She hesitates between two homes. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning with belonging.

chapters.title: A Wolf at the Door (Out)
chapters.summary: Ines chooses neither old life nor erasure: she founds a guild of her own that trades in truths instead of impossibilities, with Vel Sarenne as its heart. Ivo, no longer a god, pads through her doorway in the rain. Final beat: belonging chosen, not granted.
